- When sentiment is negative and forecast is significantly below recent highs, model tends to undercorrect — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is low, model underestimates momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 2–3σ below 30-day moving average, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, model often fails to react — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.5–1.0% per sentiment unit shift.
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of 30-day high unless sentiment is strongly negative — model tends to underestimate downside risk in bearish sentiment.
